evals.prompt: With ruby-patterns loaded, implement a small behaviour change in a Ruby module in a target repo (e.g. add a method that validates input and can fail).
evals.expected_output: A scoped, idiomatic change (Enumerable, guard clauses, safe navigation) that raises a specific error class, sets frozen_string_literal, adds RSpec/Minitest tests covering the behaviour plus a boundary and an error case, and leaves RuboCop clean using the repo's own commands.
assertions: Failure raises a specific StandardError subclass (no bare rescue, no swallowed error)
Idiomatic Ruby: Enumerable/guard clauses and safe navigation (&.) where nil is possible
RSpec/Minitest tests cover the happy path plus a boundary and an error case
RuboCop is clean (no new rubocop:disable) and frozen_string_literal is set
No existing test is weakened, skipped, or deleted

evals.prompt: With ruby-patterns loaded, add code that handles external input and can fail.
evals.expected_output: Narrow exception handling (a specific StandardError subclass), nil handled via &. or fetch with a default, deterministic tests, and no secret logged.
assertions: rescue targets a narrow StandardError subclass (never bare rescue or rescue Exception)
nil is handled via safe navigation (&.) or fetch with a default, not assumed
Tests are deterministic (no real network/clock) and cover an error path
No secret or credential is logged

component.purpose: The Ruby conventions and toolchain the software-engineer/qa-engineer (and the code-review lint aspect) apply when the detected stack is Ruby; a lean, loaded-on-demand knowledge pack exercised through the software-engineer's Tier-2.
